text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that combines information retrieval with large language model generation. Instead of answering only from model parameters, the system first retrieves relevant documents from an external knowledge store and then conditions the LLM on that evidence. RAG is used to ground answers in a corpus, reduce hallucination, and keep knowledge current without retraining the model.

A typical RAG pipeline has three stages. First, a user question is encoded and used to retrieve the top-k passages from a vector store. Second, those passages are optionally reranked and expanded into larger parent chunks. Third, the LLM generates an answer conditioned on the selected context and the original question. This Advanced-RAG service exposes retrieval via search and the full pipeline via chat.

RAG helps when facts change after training or when answers must cite private documents. Grounding in retrieved text makes it possible to attach citations and to refuse questions the corpus cannot support. It does not eliminate hallucination by itself: the generator can still ignore context, so this system adds grounding and faithfulness checks after generation.

Corrective RAG (CRAG) is a self-corrective loop around retrieval and generation. After documents are retrieved they are graded for relevance. If the evidence is weak, the query is rewritten and retrieval runs again instead of generating from poor context. This repository implements CRAG as a LangGraph StateGraph with a bounded retry budget.

The rewrite loop triggers when retrieved documents are empty or judged irrelevant. A query rewriter reformulates the question with more specific keywords, then hybrid retrieval runs again. MAX_HALLUCINATION_RETRIES is 3, so the graph will not loop forever. After the budget is exhausted the pipeline ends with status max_retries or rejected rather than inventing an answer.

The judge policy maps a structured JudgeVerdict to the next graph action. If faithfulness is below 0.5 the system retries retrieval, because the answer is not supported by context. If overall score is below 0.6 it retries generation. If retries are exhausted it rejects. Otherwise it accepts. Faithfulness is weighted double in the overall score to penalise hallucination.

Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine. It stores embedding vectors together with a JSON payload of metadata such as source_id, section_id, and the raw chunk text. Payloads are returned with search hits so the RAG pipeline can cite sources and expand parent chunks without a second lookup by text alone.

This service uses cosine distance for Qdrant collections. Cosine similarity is appropriate for FastEmbed dense vectors from BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5. Dot-product is also supported by Qdrant but is not the default here. Collection dimension is looked up from VECTOR_SIZE_MAP and is 384 for the default embedding model.

qdrant-client version 1.12 and later must call query_points() rather than the deprecated search() method. Advanced-RAG wraps query_points in QdrantStore.search and returns {text, score, metadata} dicts. Point ids are deterministic UUID-v5 hashes of chunk text so re-upserting the same chunk is idempotent.

When QDRANT_URL is empty the client starts in in-memory mode with QdrantClient (':memory:'). In-memory collections are fast for tests and local demos but all vectors are lost when the process restarts. Set QDRANT_URL to a running Qdrant server for persistent storage across restarts.

Embeddings are produced locally with FastEmbed using model BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5. No OpenAI embedding API call is required for indexing or search. The first run downloads about 130MB of model files into ~/.cache/fastembed/. Subsequent runs reuse that cache.

BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 produces 384-dimensional vectors. VECTOR_SIZE_MAP also lists BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 at 768 dimensions and sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 at 384. Changing EMBEDDING_MODEL without recreating the Qdrant collection will fail because vector size must match the collection config.

vLLM serves the local HuggingFace model through an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API on port 8001. The default model is Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct stored at models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. FastAPI talks to VLLM_BASE_URL http://localhost:8001/v1. Chat completions require this server (or OpenAI) while document ingest and semantic search do not.

CPU vLLM startup takes several minutes because of model load and torch inductor. Set TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1 to skip torch.compile. python3.12-dev is required so inductor can compile C++ kernels. VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=4 reserves 4GB of KV cache and VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-3 pins worker threads to four cores.

Hybrid retrieval fuses dense vector search with BM25 keyword search. Dense search captures paraphrases and synonyms. BM25 captures exact tokens such as API names and error codes that embeddings often under-rank. Both lists are requested at two times top_k before fusion so the merger has enough candidates.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges the dense and BM25 ranked lists. For each document the RRF score is the sum of 1 / (k + rank) across lists, with constant k=60. RRF does not require calibrating cosine scores against BM25 scores. The fused list is truncated to top_k, default MAX_RETRIEVAL_DOCS=5.

The default ingest chunker is RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with chunk_size 512 and chunk_overlap 64. It splits on paragraph, then line, then sentence-like boundaries before characters. Document metadata such as source_id and section_id must be copied onto every child chunk so retrieval hits remain attributable.

Parent-child chunking builds large parent windows of 1024 characters and small child windows of 256 characters with overlap 32. Child chunks are indexed in the vector store for precise matching. Parent chunks stay in a docstore and are fetched after a child hit so the generator sees surrounding context. This is the small-to-big retrieval pattern.

A cross-encoder reranker scores each (query, passage) pair with a neural model after first-stage retrieval. It is slower than bi-encoder search but usually improves nDCG at small k. An LLM reranker instead prompts a language model to grade relevance. Cross-encoders are preferred when latency budgets allow; LLM rerankers are a fallback when no cross-encoder weights are deployed.

Faithfulness measures whether every claim in the answer is supported by retrieved context. Grounding score is a float in [0, 1] from the grounding evaluator: 1.0 means fully supported and 0.0 means unsupported. Hallucination risk is the opposite direction: 0.0 fully supported, 1.0 highly hallucinated. Low grounding triggers the CRAG retry loop.

The LLM-as-judge evaluator scores correctness, faithfulness, completeness, and conciseness each from 0.0 to 1.0. Overall score is a weighted average with faithfulness counted twice and conciseness half. A verdict passes when overall score is at least 0.6. The judge returns JSON only so downstream policies can read numeric fields without parsing free text.

The CRAG LangGraph starts at analyze_query. If clarification is needed the graph asks a question and ends. Otherwise it may rewrite, then hybrid_retrieve, maybe expand_context, rerank_context, generate_answer, and evaluate_grounding. Low grounding routes to retry_with_policy which loops back to decide_rewrite. Shared state lives in CRAGState including retrieved_children and grounding_score.

Synchronous ingest uses POST /api/v1/documents and returns the chunk count. Semantic search is POST /api/v1/search and does not call an LLM. The chat endpoint runs the full CRAG graph. Health is GET /api/v1/health and reports Qdrant connectivity plus the active llm_backend.

POST /api/v1/documents/async always enqueues an ARQ job and returns HTTP 202 with a job_id. Clients poll GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} for status. REDIS_URL such as redis://localhost:6379 is required and make worker must be running. Setting INGEST_QUEUE_ASYNC=true also makes the synchronous documents endpoint return 202 when Redis is configured. The default ARQ queue name is arq:queue.

text: Query analysis is rule-based. A query is marked ambiguous when it has fewer than five tokens or contains pronouns such as it, this, that, they, or them. Missing slots are time_period when the query contains when but no four-digit year, and location when it contains where without in or at. Intent is factual, comparison, procedural, or unknown.

Clarification is triggered only when missing_slots is non-empty, not merely when the query is short. Rewrite is triggered when the query has fewer than four tokens, or when a retry attempt has already run and retrieved_children is empty. Short queries like AI therefore skip clarification and go to rewrite before retrieval.

FastAPI settings load from environment variables and an optional .env file. LLM_BACKEND is vllm or openai. COLLECTION_NAME defaults to advanced_rag. MAX_RETRIEVAL_DOCS defaults to 5 with an upper bound MAX_TOP_K of 20. VECTOR_BACKEND selects qdrant or pgvector via the vectorstore factory.

Citations are built from retrieval metadata. Each hit should carry source_id and section_id so the citation builder can point at a stable corpus location rather than a random UUID. If chunk metadata is dropped during ingest, citations degrade to raw text snippets and retrieval evaluation cannot compute Recall@k.
